I've seen this happening on local runs as well; we suspected it might be related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/55979
Triage: we should investigate to confirm if it's https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/55979. Either way, we should at least put a mitigation in stress to not to fail the test in this case.

Unfortunately, this is still happening. I see 4 occurrences out of 22 runs in the last 30 days. It wasn't this frequent before, is it possible that #84793 made it worse? Or could it be a server-side issue? /cc @ManickaP

Revert of the hack is up in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/87926. When it starts manifesting in the original way, we can mitigate that with targeted error handling.

Looking at the error in more detail, this is something else. It's not timeout. If you look bellow the exception you can see it's mostly not cancelled and very fast:
```
Duration: 00:00:00.0010132, Cancelled: False
```
All three errors are the same, just coming from a different operation and they are the same with or without the hack. This is completely new problem that might have started occurring at similar time as we merged https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/84793. But right know I'm not convinced this was caused by this.

Also, AFAIR, the original error was the server dropping connections due to overload, i.e. `System.Net.Quic.QuicException : Connection has been shutdown by transport. Error Code: CONNECTION_REFUSED`. I will re-close this issue and create a new one for the cancellation error we're now seeing.

review_comments: is it possible that there is image without MsQuic?
What do you mean? If you are suspecting lack of msquic as the root cause of this error - it's not the case. Removing code messing with MsQuicLibraryVersion makes things work (= HTTP/3 stress runs).

> is it possible that there is image without MsQuic?

In that case you'd get "unknown" as the MsQuic version, the code expects that.
Another option would be to tell the trimmer to keep it there via `DynamicDependency`. And this is just one string.
We should try to clarify whether test-only usage of `DynamicDependency` is ok, without that, I prefer to defensively assume it's not.

I'm wondering if this should go somewhere to `Common/test/....` so we can avoid duplication.
It may be worth of adding explanation as this is unusual craft.
Sounds good, I'll look into it.

We should keep in mind that whatever utility helper we add, its' file has to be also copied to the container, so avoiding duplication has a higher cost in complexity here than normally. At the moment I'm undecided if it's worth it, would prefer to do the docker copying work mentioned in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/84793#discussion_r1172373409 first, planning to jump to it tomorrow.
Ok, I'm holding back. Let me know when/if I should look into it.
